newsitem.title: UK: UK sees nuclear exports breaching 600 million stg.
newsitem.headline: UK sees nuclear exports breaching 600 million stg.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it saw opportunities to export more than the 600 million pounds worth of nuclear technology it sold in 1995 as countries with atomic programmes seek to diversify supplies and upgrade systems.

Speaking at a British Nuclear Congress five months after the the controversial privatisation of nuclear generator British Energy, Energy Minister Lord Fraser of Carmyllie said the global cost of decommissioning and waste management could amount to 600 billion pounds.

Lord Fraser said that while the nuclear industry should not underestimate its challenges, there were clear commercial benefits from large-scale financial assistance programmes needed to boost safety improvements in eastern Europe, Russia, Ukraine and other republics.

"Decommissioning is a relatively new field in which Britain has much to offer," he said. "There have already been British successes, with BNFL (state-owned British Nuclear Fuels) winning over $1.0 billion business in the United States."

But he noted that commercial success and continued safe operation were "inextricably linked", noting that the government would continue to take a close interest in the "safety, security and prosperity" of the nuclear industry.
